Silicon Valley Capital Partners increased its stake in shares of Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 5.0% in the second quarter, HoldingsChannel reports. The firm owned 31,978 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after buying an additional 1,531 shares during the quarter. Apple comprises approximately 2.9% of Silicon Valley Capital Partners’ investment portfolio, making the stock its 7th biggest position. Silicon Valley Capital Partners’ holdings in Apple were worth $6,085,000 as of its most recent SEC filing.
A number of other hedge funds also recently added to or reduced their stakes in the stock. Investment Partners LTD. increased its position in Apple by 4.9% during the 2nd quarter. Investment Partners LTD. now owns 5,594 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $1,036,000 after purchasing an additional 263 shares during the period. Keating Investment Counselors Inc. increased its position in Apple by 8.2% during the 2nd quarter. Keating Investment Counselors Inc. now owns 3,511 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $650,000 after purchasing an additional 266 shares during the period. Townsend & Associates Inc increased its position in Apple by 6.8% during the 2nd quarter. Townsend & Associates Inc now owns 4,204 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $778,000 after purchasing an additional 268 shares during the period. Dorsey Wright & Associates increased its position in Apple by 9.2% during the 2nd quarter. Dorsey Wright & Associates now owns 3,205 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $593,000 after purchasing an additional 270 shares during the period. Finally, Taylor Cottrill Erickson & Associates Inc. boosted its stake in Apple by 0.5% in the 2nd quarter. Taylor Cottrill Erickson & Associates Inc. now owns 57,634 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $10,669,000 after purchasing an additional 270 shares in the last quarter. Institutional investors and hedge funds own 57.65% of the company’s stock. Get Apple alerts:
A number of equities analysts recently issued reports on AAPL shares. Citigroup dropped their price target on shares of Apple from $265.00 to $240.00 and set a “buy” rating on the stock in a research note on Friday, November 2nd. Morgan Stanley upped their price target on shares of Apple from $226.00 to $253.00 and gave the stock an “overweight” rating in a research note on Thursday, November 8th. Royal Bank of Canada set a $240.00 price target on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Monday, September 24th. Wells Fargo & Co reiterated a “neutral” rating and issued a $210.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research note on Friday, August 10th. Finally, JPMorgan Chase & Co. started coverage on shares of Apple in a research note on Thursday, September 27th. They issued an “overweight” rating and a $272.00 price target on the stock. Four equities research analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, twenty-two have issued a hold rating and twenty-five have assigned a buy rating to the company’s stock. The stock has an average rating of “Hold” and a consensus price target of $221.30. In related news, insider Chris Kondo sold 3,408 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction on Monday, November 19th. The stock was sold at an average price of $190.00, for a total value of $647,520.00. Following the completion of the sale, the insider now directly owns 8,940 shares in the company, valued at $1,698,600. The sale was disclosed in a filing with the SEC, which can be accessed through this link . Also, SVP Angela J. Ahrendts sold 25,000 shares of the firm’s stock in a transaction on Wednesday, October 3rd. The stock was sold at an average price of $232.66, for a total value of $5,816,500.00. Following the completion of the sale, the senior vice president now owns 105,538 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $24,554,471.08. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders have sold a total of 204,845 shares of company stock valued at $47,015,677 over the last quarter. Corporate insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock.
Shares of AAPL opened at $180.94 on Thursday. The company has a quick ratio of 1.09, a current ratio of 1.12 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87. Apple Inc. has a 1 year low of $150.24 and a 1 year high of $233.47. The company has a market cap of $856.41 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 15.19, a P/E/G ratio of 1.25 and a beta of 1.26.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its quarterly earnings data on Thursday, November 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.91 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, beating analysts’ consensus estimates of $2.78 by $0.13. Apple had a net margin of 22.41% and a return on equity of 48.68%. The business had revenue of $62.90 billion during the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $61.55 billion. During the same period last year, the firm posted $2.07 EPS. The company’s revenue was up 19.6% on a year-over-year basis. Analysts forecast that Apple Inc. will post 13.35 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
The company also recently announced a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, November 15th. Stockholders of record on Monday, November 12th were given a dividend of $0.73 per share. The ex-dividend date was Thursday, November 8th. This represents a $2.92 dividend on an annualized basis and a dividend yield of 1.61%. Apple’s dividend payout ratio is currently 24.52%.
Apple Profile
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers. It also sells various related software, services, accessories, and third-party digital content and applications. The company offers iPhone, a line of smartphones; iPad, a line of multi-purpose tablets; and Mac, a line of desktop and portable personal computers, as well as iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS operating systems.
